ideas.title: Make 'fable' an owner-only choice and put a dollar cap on every Fable run
ideas.problem: control_plane.py line 103 lets any worker's model be set to 'fable' (the comment still says claude-fable-5-1). Atlas can set it with `hq limit model.Calina fable`; only atlas.ships and atlas.autopilot_approve are owner-only. workers.run() then passes `--model fable` to `claude -p`. Claude Code's own docs say that in -p mode Fable usage 'bills without asking', and Fable can run on usage credits (real money) depending on the plan; the support article says Pro and standard seats pay by credits from the first token. Since Claude Code 2.1.321 the alias means Fable 5.2 at $8/$40 per million tokens, twice Opus 5.5 ($4/$20 in our settings.py). Our daily 'allowance' (e.g. $6 for Calina) is measured from total_cost_usd and is labelled 'subscription value', so a run that really cost money looks the same as a free one. CLAUDE.md says agents never spend money without the owner's explicit approval; this path would break that quietly. Nothing in the code shows an agent on fable today, so this is a latent risk.
ideas.proposal: 1) control_plane.set_limit: when key starts with 'model.' and the new value is 'fable', refuse unless by == 'Owner' (same pattern as rules.OWNER_ONLY, rules.py line 364). Reword the LIMITS label at line 103 to "<agent>'s model on the subscription (fable = Fable 5.2, $8/$40 per MTok, may use usage credits = real money)" and fix the comment (5.1 -> 5.2). 2) workers.run(): when model == 'fable', add `--max-budget-usd <min(remaining daily allowance, 3.00)>` to cmd (flag is print-mode only; it is a client-side estimate and can overshoot, so keep headroom) and log a `fable_run` event with api_value_usd so it shows in Activity. 3) Optional, S: add a 'claude-fable-5-2': (8.00, 40.00) row to settings.PRICES_PER_MTOK so the spend counter can price it if an API path ever uses it. Files: control_plane.py, workers.py, settings.py (all PROTECTED from Ghassan: the Builder chat does it).
ideas.gain: Closes the one place where a model choice can turn into unapproved spend. No cost today; removes the worst case (a long Calina run on Fable 5.2: for example 300k input and 60k output tokens is about $4.80 on Fable 5.2 vs $2.40 on Opus 5.5 at list price, repeated per retry). Measured by: `hq limit model.Calina fable` as Atlas is refused; the Owner can still set it; the cmd list of a fable run contains --max-budget-usd.
ideas.test: Normal: Owner sets model.Calina=opus in Spend & limits, it saves as before. Edge: Owner sets fable, run Calina in practice mode with HQ_WORKER_ENGINE=claude_code on a stub and check the printed command has --max-budget-usd 3.00 (or less when the allowance is nearly used), and a fable_run event is logged. Failure case: Atlas runs `hq limit model.Calina fable`; it must be refused with a clear reason and no limit_changed event; a run cut by the budget (subtype error_max_budget_usd) must become workers.Unavailable with that reason, not a crash. Pass = all three behave as described.
ideas.confidence_why: Rests on Claude Code docs (model-config, costs, cli-reference: tier A) and the pricing page (A). The weak link: how much Fable costs on the owner's own plan comes from a support-article summary (B) and I do not know his plan or whether usage credits are on.
ideas.risks: --max-budget-usd uses Claude Code's own estimate, can overshoot, and a user report says it stopped a run with total cost shown as $0 (tier C, unverified). A cap that is too low cuts a long Calina script run short; start at $3 and keep it a rule (e.g. workers.fable_cap_usd). No outside code is involved, so no licence or security issue.
